metadata.title: Technical Feasibility of Reporting YITS 2010 Skill Assessment Results on the PISA 2000 Reading Scale (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Youth in Transition Survey (YITS) 2010 PISA reassessment sample and applies population weights calculated by Statistics Canada to make the YITS reassessment sample representative of the population represented by the PISA/YITS 2000 sample. The final YITS PISA reassessment weight is constructed as the product of (i) an adjustment for subsampling of the Cycle 5 YITS sample, (ii) a non-response adjustment based on logistic regression response probabilities within regions, and (iii) a calibration adjustment to align weighted totals with Cycle 5 gender totals. The paper states that these weights are used for all analyses presented. Replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are not described, so uncertainty estimation is not specified in the excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample consists of YITS Cycle 5 respondents in Canada who were selected for the YITS PISA reassessment (approximately 2,000 selected) and who actually completed the PISA-linked reading assessment booklet (1,297 completed). The reassessment uses a single 60-minute booklet containing 28 PISA 2000 link items (with items grouped into two clusters in fixed order). For conditioning-variable principal component scoring, missing values in the conditioning variables are replaced by the sample mean.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD technical study evaluates whether YITS 2010 respondents (age ~25) can be scored on the PISA 2000 reading proficiency scale using a subset of PISA 2000 reading link items. The authors administer 28 PISA 2000 items to a YITS reassessment subsample and examine item suitability and test functioning across the older population, focusing on whether there is a ceiling effect and whether item difficulty patterns remain consistent. They scale YITS item responses onto the PISA 2000 reading scale using the PISA 2000 item parameter framework, treat “not-reached” responses as not applicable (missing at random) for proficiency estimation, and generate plausible values (10 per respondent) to support secondary analyses. They also replicate the conditioning and plausible-value generation logic using a reduced set of conditioning variables (principal component scores) and discuss limitations for interpreting YITS scores as “true PISA results,” including higher measurement variance due to fewer items and the need for careful variance estimation when computing change between PISA 2000 and YITS 2010.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a feasibility/technical scaling report rather than an empirical machine-learning prediction study. As such, it does not train or compare ML algorithms, and it does not report ML-style performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC) for predictive targets. The extraction therefore leaves ML fields empty and uses the outcome summary to describe the assessment scaling procedures, item functioning checks, and implications for reporting comparably scaled reading proficiency.
